mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact corporate earnings and thus drive up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but SPX returns are negative over the 20-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate revenues, driving up S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 4% but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low, consumer confidence and spending increase, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both GDPC1 growth and UNRATE are favorable but SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A high CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL is high but SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic activity, which should positively impact corporate revenues and drive up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO is above 100 but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: When both retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) increase, consumer demand is strong, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both RSAFS and HOUST are increasing but SPX returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates tighter monetary policy, which may negatively impact corporate borrowing costs and lead to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is rising but SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which should lead to increased consumer spending and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS is above 140000 but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 20-day periods.
